; Reset sound-effect channel ownership and active stream pointers through the bank-local entry.
; Request an effect: A supplies priority, X selects the descriptor; lower-priority requests may be rejected.
; Three sound entry jumps precede the music command entry. A >= $80 selects channel shutdown;
; smaller values select a five-pointer song record.
; Clear music ownership for four channels and write the retained $E0 enable mask to the APU. No
; song meaning is implied.
; Select five split-byte pointers using song index times five. Initialize four stream delays and
; channel flags. The later tick accumulates tempo and updates four channels only on carry; $8102
; receives Y=channel and X=APU register stride.
; Add the channel transpose to the decoded note token; carry comes from the preceding token comparison.
; Translate the note to timer bytes, consume duration/instrument nibbles, and advance the main
; stream by two. Instrument flags choose short or extended modulation-pointer layouts; three
; modulation streams have independent countdowns.
; Update the first modulation stream only when its per-channel countdown expires.
; An absent high pointer or $80 token leaves the register unchanged. Otherwise merge the next low
; nibble into the cached channel control byte.
; Mark the control byte dirty, load its hold duration, and advance this modulation pointer by two bytes.
; Run the timer-low modulation stream when its countdown expires.
; Read a delta/duration stream: zero holds, $80 redirects the pointer, and other bytes add to timer-low.
; Complete the little-endian stream redirect and retry after one tick.
; Add the signed modular delta to the cached timer-low byte.
; Schedule a timer-low APU write.
; Use the second byte as the stream countdown.
; Advance the pitch-delta stream by two bytes with carry.
; Run the note-offset modulation stream only on countdown expiry.
; Load the note-offset stream; $80 redirects to another little-endian pointer.
; Complete the note-offset redirect and defer consumption by one tick.
; Add the modulation byte to the base note and translate to timer-high while retaining cached control bits.
; Translate timer-low, mark both timer bytes dirty, reload duration, and advance the note-offset stream.
; Test channel state before committing cached register changes.
; Return without touching APU registers.
; Dirty bits 0,1,2 select timer-high, timer-low and control writes. Clear each bit after writing
; through Y, the channel register stride.
; Separate high-byte then low-byte arrays form six handler addresses in sound pair3 (physical
; banks6/7). MusicDispatchControlToken combines the corresponding bytes; this is not a table of
; physical offsets.
; six split-byte sound-control handler pointer pairs83B7..83C3.
; Tokens >= $60 index split-byte handler tables, then dispatch through a RAM pointer. Table extent
; and additional handlers remain unclassified.
; Clear the low control nibble when required, derive hold duration from the shared duration
; pointer, then advance the command stream.
; Retain the effect-ownership bit, silence cached music registers, then continue channel finalization.
; Resolve a phrase selector through split pointers and set transpose. The following repeat path
; saves or restores the return stream and decrements a repetition counter.
; Mark the saved phrase return as active.
; Rewind the channel's music stream pointer by four bytes, propagating borrow to its high byte.
; Join the shared token continuation; this changes the stream position, not an APU period.
; Clear repeat/transpose state and restart channel decoding. The later jump token replaces the
; main stream with an encoded little-endian address.
; Read the duration-table word from control-stream bytes 1 and 2, then prime this channel's note
; countdown to one. Continues the repeat/jump token handler in sound bank6.
; Advance the main stream by Y+1, preserving carry into its high byte; restore channel index and
; register stride.
; Zero timer-low and control, mask timer-high, and mark all three cached registers dirty.
; Sound data under physical banks6/7: period bytes, split instrument/song/phrase pointers and
; music streams. Existing Music/Sound table aliases identify the directly consumed bases. Token
; grammar and subdivisions beyond those consumers remain unresolved; generic bytes are
; intentionally retained.
; sound timer/instrument/song/phrase tables and music byte streams; generic non-code where exact
; subformat unproved.
; Clear active effect pointers, priorities, and the shared APU enable shadow for four channels.
; Save request priority and descriptor index. Decode the target channel and reject invalid
; channels or requests below its current priority.
; Restore the caller stack value and return without replacing the effect.
; Claim the channel, suspend its music ownership, initialize delay and cached period/control,
; flush initial registers, then point past the five-byte effect header.
; Return from the invalid-descriptor path; surrounding stack contract remains uncertain.
; Visit all four channels. Each active effect advances only after its delay reaches zero.
; Consume one effect delay tick.
; Return while the effect remains delayed.
; A zero stream high byte marks an inactive effect.
; Read the next effect duration; $FF terminates the stream.
; Store duration and control, clear dirty flags, then inspect the next period byte. A $FF period
; requests an effect restart.
; Recover the saved request index and current priority, then re-enter effect selection.
; Channel three compares and updates the noise period without tonal high-byte handling.
; Update the cached tonal high-period byte only when changed; the following unclassified bytes remain literal.
; Mark the channel tone-high register for refresh without disturbing other pending register
; writes.
; Compare the next stream byte with cached timer-low; neighboring unclassified flag updates remain unresolved.
; Mark the channel tone-low register for refresh.
; Advance the effect stream; nonzero cached period commits dirty registers, otherwise end the effect.
